title: The Zodiac's Cipher Was Cracked After 51 Years

lines.text: The Zodiac Killer mailed this. For fifty-one years, nobody could read it.
Three hundred forty symbols.
Mailed to the San Francisco Chronicle in 1969.
The Zodiac killed at least five people in Northern California.
His first cipher fell in about a week.
This one didn't.
Then, in December 2020, three amateurs broke it.
A software developer in Virginia.
A mathematician in Australia.
A programmer in Belgium.
Their key insight: it wasn't written left to right.
Most of it ran diagonally. Down one row, across two.
The mathematician tested hundreds of thousands of reading orders.
The Belgian's program attacked each one.
Then, real English surfaced.
The FBI acknowledged the cipher had been solved.
So what did it say?
I hope you are having lots of fun in trying to catch me.
That wasn't me on the TV show.
Probably a 1969 TV caller who claimed to be him.
Fifty-one years of waiting. For a taunt.
No name. The killer has never been identified.
And two shorter Zodiac ciphers remain unsolved.
One is just thirteen symbols. Right before it, he wrote: my name is.
Think you can read it?

shots.description: CIPHER GRID PROP (build once, reuse): 20 rows x 17 columns = 340 glyph cells laid out on a flat plane, each cell a text3d glyph (extrude 0.01) in dark ink on an aged off-white paper plane. Glyphs are STAND-INS drawn from DejaVu/Oswald (Latin capitals, some mirrored or rotated 90/180 deg, a few Greek letters, dots, slashes, triangles) arranged so the page reads like the 1969 sheet without claiming to reproduce it symbol-for-symbol. Every glyph is its own object so it can be keyframed (emission, colour, position). Frame 1: extreme close-up already drifting across rows of glyphs on the paper; by 1.5 s the camera has pulled back to reveal the whole 20x17 block floating in black; cells flicker faint red as if being scanned.
shots.camera: starts macro 85mm sliding along a row, fast ease-out pull-back to full grid by 1.5 s, slight handheld amp 0.01
shots.lighting: single soft top-light on the paper, deep black surround, faint red emission pulses on random glyphs
fx: fine dust motes in the light

shots.description: Counting beat: the camera tilts across the full grid while each row of glyphs blinks white in sequence top to bottom as the counter runs.
shots.camera: top-down 35mm, fast tilt row by row

shots.description: Stylised 1969 newsroom (room builder: long desks with box typewriters, hanging cone lamps, venetian-blind window with night city glow). A faceless clerk silhouette slits open a plain envelope (no real address/handwriting) and a folded sheet with the cipher-grid texture slides onto the desk under a lamp.
shots.camera: slow overhead crane down onto the desk, 35mm
characters: newsroom clerk silhouette (char_figure, shirt + tie, faceless)
shots.lighting: warm tungsten desk lamps, cigarette-haze, cool blue window spill

shots.description: Respect beat, no crime scenes: a dark map card of the San Francisco Bay Area coast; five small white candle-like points fade in one by one at neutral spots in the region (not exact sites). No names of places of death, no imagery of victims.
shots.camera: 2D overlay over a very dark fog plate; slow push

overlay.text:
At least five people killed
Case still open

shots.description: Document reveal on a kitchen-table plate (warm lamp, two coffee cups as simple cylinders): a 1969-style newspaper column slides in, with a smaller earlier cipher sheet under it; pencil-drawn solving marks over its symbols. On 'This one didn't' (about 2.3 s in) the paper whips away and the defocused 340 grid slams back in behind red text.
shots.camera: 2D overlay over the kitchen-table plate, slight push

overlay.text:
First Zodiac cipher (408 symbols)
mailed July 1969
solved about a week later
by a Salinas couple

shots.description: Three vertical panels side by side, each a small dark room lit only by a computer monitor (box monitor + keyboard, modern flat screen glow): a faceless silhouette at each desk. Monitors show scrolling grids of letters. Panels slide in left-right-left.
shots.camera: three static 35mm frames, each with a slow push; panels slide in with a whip
characters: solver silhouette C (all faceless, no likeness)
shots.lighting: cool blue-white monitor glow on each silhouette, room otherwise black

shots.description: World map card: pin drops on Virginia (USA); solver card A slides in. Background plate: solver silhouette A's monitor glow, defocused.
shots.camera: 2D overlay; map zoom on North America

overlay.text:
DAVID ORANCHAK
software developer - Virginia, USA

shots.description: Route line jumps from Virginia across the Pacific to Melbourne; pin drops; card B.
shots.camera: 2D overlay; map pans with the line

overlay.text:
SAM BLAKE
applied mathematician - Melbourne, Australia

shots.description: Route line jumps north-west to Belgium; pin drops; card C. All three pins now visible linked by a red triangle.
shots.camera: 2D overlay; map pulls back to the whole world

overlay.text:
JARL VAN EYCKE
programmer, author of AZdecrypt - Belgium

All three: amateur codebreakers
working together online

shots.description: METHOD TURN. The cipher grid returns, sharp. A white reading-arrow sweeps left-to-right along row 1, then stops, flashes red and shatters into fragments.
shots.camera: frontal 50mm, quick push-in on row 1
shots.lighting: cold top-light; red flash on the arrow break

shots.description: Letters rearranging: starting at the top-left glyph, a glowing red path hops down 1 row and right 2 columns, wrapping at the edge; each visited glyph lifts out of the grid and slides into a new straight line at the bottom of frame, forming a re-ordered strip. The grid splits into three horizontal sections (rows 1-9, 10-18, 19-20) with thin gaps.
shots.camera: top-down 35mm, slight tilt to show glyphs lifting in depth
shots.lighting: glyphs on the path emit red; rest dimmed to 30%
fx: thin light trails along the path

shots.description: Close on a modern monitor in a dark room: dozens of tiny thumbnail grids, each a different hop-pattern, flicker past in a mosaic; screen glow fills the frame and reflects on a desk.
shots.camera: slow push into the screen, 50mm, until the mosaic fills frame
characters: solver silhouette B (shoulder only, out of focus)
shots.lighting: monitor glow cyan-white, everything else black

overlay.text:
HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS
OF READING ORDERS

shots.description: Second monitor, different room colour (amber desk lamp + screen): a program window (generic UI, labelled 'AZdecrypt' as plain text, no real screenshots) shows a score bar climbing and candidate plaintext lines scrolling as gibberish.
shots.camera: over-the-shoulder 35mm, slow orbit 10 deg

overlay.text:
AZdecrypt - solver software
written by Van Eycke

shots.description: MID-POINT TURN (unreadable becomes readable). Decode cascade: on the screen the gibberish lines freeze; letters in one line flip like split-flap cells until a fragment reads as clean English, glowing red, while the rest of the line stays noise. Use a fragment of the published plaintext (e.g. LOTS OF FUN); do not imply which words appeared first.
shots.camera: locked-off macro on the screen line, tiny push
shots.lighting: red text glow dominates; monitor dim

shots.description: Document reveal: a neutral recreated statement card (no FBI seal, no letterhead) slides up; a red stamp hits.
shots.camera: 2D overlay over the blurred grid plate

overlay.text:
The FBI said a cipher attributed to
the Zodiac Killer had been solved
by private citizens.
(paraphrase, 11 Dec 2020)

shots.description: The full 340 grid; all glyphs begin to flip toward letters at once, freezing halfway (left half symbols, right half letters) as the line ends.
shots.camera: slow push-in, 50mm, centred
shots.lighting: cold blue → warm amber colour-temperature shift sweeping left to right

shots.description: Decoded text typed onto aged paper, line by line, over the half-flipped grid plate.
shots.camera: 2D overlay, slight push

overlay.text:
I HOPE YOU ARE HAVING LOTS OF FUN
IN TRYING TO CATCH ME

shots.description: A 1969 box TV set (rounded box, wood veneer, convex screen) alone in a dark room, screen showing a grainy talk-show set: two faceless chair silhouettes and a desk phone. Static rolls across.
shots.camera: slow push toward the screen, 35mm
fx: static noise on the screen texture

overlay.text:
"THAT WASN'T ME
ON THE TV SHOW"

shots.description: Same TV, screen now shows a big old rotary-desk-phone icon lit up; captions on screen 'LIVE CALL-IN'.
shots.camera: tighter on the screen, 50mm

overlay.text:
Oct 1969: a caller to a live TV show
claimed to be the Zodiac

shots.description: Anticlimax beat: the decoded grid of letters slowly dims to grey; one glowing letter at a time switches off.
shots.camera: very slow pull-back, 50mm

shots.description: Recreated case-file cover (no real seal): 'ZODIAC - UNIDENTIFIED' typed; a stamp 'OPEN' lands.
shots.camera: 2D overlay over dark desk plate

overlay.text:
SUSPECT: UNIDENTIFIED
No one has been charged
Status: OPEN

shots.description: Two small glyph strips (13 cells and 32 cells, same stand-in glyph style) rise out of the dark below the big grid, outlined in red.
shots.camera: tilt down from the big grid to the two strips, 35mm

shots.description: Paper scrap with 'MY NAME IS —' typed, then the 13 stand-in glyphs type on after it, one by one.
shots.camera: 2D overlay, push-in to the glyph row

shots.description: Loop frame: the camera slides back into the macro row-drift framing of S01 over the big grid, glyphs flickering red — frame matches S01 frame 1.
shots.camera: matches S01: macro 85mm row drift

overlay.text:
In memory of the Zodiac's victims
